## Fernando de Noronha tours: which itinerary should you choose?

**If the [Fernando de Noronha](/brazil/place/fernando-de-noronha/) archipelago is your main destination, choose by the number of island days rather than the total trip length.** In the Ada Tours catalog, you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that visit this destination on their main itineraries. The stops, scheduled activities and domestic flight arrangements differ.

The [10-day journey through northeastern Brazil](/brazil/tour/northeast-brazil-recife-porto-de-galinhas-fernando-de-noronha-10-days/) devotes days 5–10 to the islands, including arrival and departure. It features a four-wheel-drive excursion, scheduled diving and 2 free days on Noronha. The [13-day Brazil tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-paradise-private-tour-13-days/) reaches the archipelago only on day 10, after Rio, Iguazu, Recife and Porto de Galinhas. On the islands, a 4x4 tour and a free day are planned, with optional activities at sea.

| Criterion | 10 days | 13 days |
|---|---|---|
| Main focus | Beaches of the northeast | Extensive Brazil itinerary |
| Time on Noronha | Days 5–10 | Days 10–13 |
| Diving | Scheduled day | Optional activity |
| Recife–Noronha | Flights included | Domestic flights excluded |
| Island sightseeing | 4x4 | 4x4 |

Compare the conditions of both specific tours. Their duration, prices and included activities are shown on their individual pages; the dynamic table below draws its information from the current catalog.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_brazil_recife_porto_noronha_10d,tour_source_rajskaya_braziliya}}

## Ten days: Recife, Porto de Galinhas and Noronha

The [private ten-day tour](/brazil/tour/northeast-brazil-recife-porto-de-galinhas-fernando-de-noronha-10-days/) begins in [Recife](/brazil/place/recife/). On the second day, travelers explore its historic neighborhoods and neighboring [Olinda](/brazil/place/olinda/). The route then continues through [Porto de Galinhas](/brazil/place/porto-de-galinhas/), where beaches and natural pools among the reefs are particular attractions. Day four is free.

On day five, the itinerary includes a flight from Recife to [Fernando de Noronha](/brazil/place/fernando-de-noronha/). The following day features a 4x4 island tour covering historic Vila dos Remédios, bays, viewpoints and beaches. The route includes places where dolphins and sea turtles may be observed, although sightings of specific animals always depend on natural conditions.

**Day seven is devoted to diving.** The itinerary describes a boat trip into the ocean and instructor-led dives for certified divers and beginners. Check eligibility, preparation and precisely which services are included under this tour's terms: a diving day on the schedule does not, by itself, confirm every expense or operator requirement. Days eight and nine are free, allowing you to return to a favorite beach, relax or book an optional activity.

An important pricing detail: **Recife–Fernando de Noronha–Recife flights are explicitly listed among the included services on the ten-day tour**. International flights, additional meals and independently arranged optional excursions are excluded. These arrangements are worth comparing with the second itinerary, where domestic flights are not included.

## Thirteen days: Rio, Iguazu and an island finale

The [13-day private Brazil tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-paradise-private-tour-13-days/) is for travelers who want to see several of the country's best-known regions in one trip. It starts in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), featuring Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado and the historic center, followed by Iguazu Falls. The trip continues to [Recife](/brazil/place/recife/) and [Olinda](/brazil/place/olinda/), then allows time in [Porto de Galinhas](/brazil/place/porto-de-galinhas/).

**Travelers arrive on Noronha on day ten.** The following day features a 4x4 island excursion through historic Vila dos Remédios, Dolphin Bay, Sancho Beach and other archipelago sites. Day twelve is free, with beaches, diving, a boat trip or trekking suggested as optional activities. A flight back to Recife is planned for day thirteen.

In this version, the islands are the finale to a broad sightseeing journey. Travelers arrive after an intensive urban and nature program, so the free day provides welcome relaxation. However, there is less scope for several extra marine excursions than on the ten-day trip.

Another difference: **domestic flights appear in the “Not Included” section of the thirteen-day tour**. Comparing only its listed price with the ten-day route without allowing for air travel would therefore be misleading. Differences in accommodation categories, guiding and excursions must also be assessed against the confirmed terms of each program.

## How many days do you actually spend on the archipelago?

Total tour length can be deceptive. Count the days you are already on the island and can enjoy beaches, diving or trails separately from the flight days.

On the ten-day tour, **arrival is on day 5 and departure on day 10**. In between are a full sightseeing excursion, a diving day and 2 free days. This works well if you want to head out on the ocean again or leave some time for relaxation when the weather is changeable.

On the thirteen-day tour, **arrival is on day 10 and departure on day 13**. The two full island days are the excursion on day 11 and free time on day 12. This option makes more sense if you want Noronha alongside other iconic places in Brazil, rather than an extended diving holiday.

| Your priority | Better fit |
|---|---|
| More time on Noronha | 10-day tour |
| Rio and Iguazu on the same trip | 13-day tour |
| A dedicated diving day | 10-day tour |
| A short island finale | 13-day tour |

If you want to compare other beach routes, visit the [Brazil beach tours catalog](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/). It covers a broader selection; not every trip there visits the archipelago.

## What to see on Fernando de Noronha

Noronha is known for its volcanic coastline, clear ocean water and protected marine ecosystems. More than one viewpoint is needed to appreciate the island: combine bays, the historic settlement, beaches, a sea excursion or diving.

**Sancho and nearby bays.** Viewpoints reveal the dramatic coastline, while beaches offer relaxation subject to sea conditions and local rules. Both itineraries explore different coastal parts of the island. Confirm in advance which sites will actually be accessible on the chosen day.

**Dolphin Bay.** The name comes from the spinner dolphins that use the bay for resting. According to the archipelago administration, they can be observed from a viewpoint above the water; entering the bay itself is prohibited. “Seeing dolphins” therefore does not mean swimming beside them or approaching the animals.

**Vila dos Remédios.** The island's historic quarter, with its church and old fortress, adds cultural interest to a beach-focused stay. Both trips include the settlement on their 4x4 sightseeing day, making it convenient to experience the archipelago's natural and historic sides in one excursion.

**Scuba diving and snorkeling.** Rays, sea turtles and various fish live around the islands. Underwater outings are interesting not only for wildlife but also for the seabed, water clarity and changing underwater scenery. Scuba diving and swimming with a mask are distinct activities. Diving requires consideration of experience, health, the instructor's requirements and sea conditions. If underwater activities are your priority, explore the [diving tours selection](/interests/diving/).

## Conservation rules and visiting arrangements

Much of the archipelago belongs to a national marine park. According to ICMBio and the visitor operator, **a separate ticket is required for entry to national park areas**, and some routes have visitor limits and require advance booking. The Atalaia trail, for example, is subject to reservation. Rules may vary by beach and activity.

Before traveling, check ticket procedures, trail availability, equipment rules and local restrictions. An included island excursion should not be assumed to cover every conservation fee and additional marine activity unless these are explicitly listed in the chosen tour's terms.

Chasing, feeding or touching wildlife is prohibited in protected areas. Natural pools have further restrictions on sunscreen products, fins and photographic equipment. These measures help protect reefs and marine life.

## When to go for beaches and diving

Fernando de Noronha can be visited in different months, but **calm seas in one bay do not guarantee calm conditions in another**. Wave direction, wind, rainfall and tides affect beach access, underwater visibility and boat departures. For diving, consider not only the calendar but also advice from the local operator for your actual travel dates.

If you want several dives, the ten-day itinerary provides more island time and free days. If Rio, Iguazu and Atlantic beaches matter most, the thirteen-day route offers wider geographical coverage. Choose a date according to your main objective and the real conditions of your selected tour.

## Frequently asked questions about Fernando de Noronha tours

### Which tour is better for diving?

The [10-day tour](/brazil/tour/northeast-brazil-recife-porto-de-galinhas-fernando-de-noronha-10-days/) has a dedicated diving day and 2 additional free days on the archipelago. On the [13-day itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-paradise-private-tour-13-days/), diving is an optional activity on a free day.

### Which itinerary includes flights to the archipelago?

The ten-day trip lists Recife–Noronha–Recife flights among the included services. On the thirteen-day itinerary, domestic air travel is excluded. This makes a significant difference when comparing budgets.

### Can you see dolphins on an island excursion?

Both programs include areas where marine wildlife can be observed. Dolphins are wild animals, however: sightings are not guaranteed, and the bay is subject to conservation restrictions. Viewing takes place from authorized platforms.

### Is a separate national marine park ticket required?

Access to the park is regulated by a separate admission ticket, while some trails need advance reservations. Check current rules before visiting and confirm which costs are included in the tour.

### Can I spend the whole holiday on Noronha without other stops?

Both published Ada Tours itineraries through the archipelago also include other parts of Brazil. If you want a holiday exclusively on Noronha, request a separate tailor-made program rather than treating it as an existing standalone catalog package.

## Florianópolis: beaches, lagoons and routes across Santa Catarina Island

Florianópolis is the capital of Santa Catarina state in southern [Brazil](/brazil/). Most of the city is located on Santa Catarina Island, connected to the mainland by bridges. Ocean beaches, dunes, lagoons, fishing villages and urban neighborhoods coexist on the island. It is therefore best to plan your Florianópolis route around **the geography and conditions of each shore**, rather than simply picking the most famous beaches from a list.

Seasonal differences are more noticeable here than at the tropical resorts of Brazil's northeast. Beaches are busy in summer, while cooler periods favor walking, nature and food. Sea conditions depend on the wind, waves and individual bay.

## Eastern island: Joaquina, Praia Mole and Lagoa da Conceição

**Joaquina** and **Praia Mole** are known for their waves and surfing culture. They appeal to travelers who enjoy open-ocean beaches, walking along broad stretches of sand and watching surfers. Strong waves, surf and currents can make swimming difficult, however; a beach well suited to surfing is not necessarily a good choice for a beginner swimmer.

**Lagoa da Conceição** has a different atmosphere, with lagoon waters, hills, shoreline vegetation and cafés. Spend part of a day away from the ocean breakers before heading to the dunes. A protected dune park preserves sandy landscapes and the coastal *restinga* ecosystem. Choose authorized walking paths, avoid trampling vegetation and remember that the heat feels stronger on exposed sand.

For activities on the dunes, including sandboarding, check protected-area rules and whether the service is available on your chosen date. The presence of dunes does not mean that board rental is included in a particular [Brazil tour](/brazil/tour/).

## North, south and central areas: why the island needs to be divided

| Part of the island | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| East | Waves, surfing and dunes |
| North | Resort bays and services |
| South | Nature and fishing communities |
| Center | Urban history and markets |

The **north** of the island has beach districts with different accommodation options and visitor facilities. These suit travelers who prefer to spend days by the water without changing hotels often. Even neighboring beaches, however, differ in wave and wind conditions.

The **south** has quieter communities and natural areas, including routes that require hiking. Before trekking, establish the distance, difficulty and return options: not every scenic viewpoint can be reached on a short stroll from the beach.

The **city center** offers historic buildings, the municipal market and squares. This is a better place to explore local culture and food than to search for the perfect ocean beach. On a short stop, choosing one natural area and a city walk may be more sensible than a long drive with numerous beach stops.

## Getting around the island: why map distances can mislead

Florianópolis is connected to the mainland, but approaches to island beaches and roads between neighborhoods can become heavily congested during peak season. A straight line on a map does not show the actual time needed to travel across bridges, hills and city streets.

If you have **one or two days**, choose nearby locations such as Lagoa da Conceição, Joaquina and other sites on the east side. With **three or four days**, alternate eastern and northern shores and leave some time for the city. A longer stay lets you explore the south and its nature routes without rushing.

For a beach hotel, decide in advance which factors matter most: walking distance to a particular beach, a choice of restaurants, surfing waves or convenient daily car trips. It is not always possible to have all of them in one location.

## Urban culture and southern Brazil

Florianópolis has much to offer beyond beaches. Its island settlements have a history shaped in part by Azorean heritage, which can be seen in certain neighborhoods and the local cuisine. Fish, seafood and coastal village traditions provide a distinct way to discover the city. The presence of restaurants and handicrafts does not mean a tasting or workshop is already included in a tour.

For a broader journey through southern Brazil, combine Florianópolis with [Curitiba](/brazil/place/curitiba/) and [Porto Alegre](/brazil/place/porto-alegre/). This reveals a progression from Santa Catarina's island beaches to the urban and regional culture of the southern states. Plan journeys between cities as separate stages; attempting to visit every city on a day trip from the island would be impractical.

## When to visit and how to prepare

Southern Hemisphere summer, including December, January and February, attracts beach travelers but is also a time of high demand. Autumn and winter are cooler and more changeable, so do not expect warm seas without checking likely conditions. Walks, photography and sightseeing are possible in different seasons with clothing suited to the forecast.

Before swimming, check lifeguard warnings and water quality at the specific beach. Santa Catarina's environmental agency publishes changing results of bathing-water monitoring. For surfing, assess waves, wind and your own experience separately.

## Frequently asked questions about Florianópolis

### Which beaches are best for surfing?

Joaquina and Praia Mole are leading options, but suitable waves depend on the day and your experience. Beginners need to select the right stretch of beach and lesson conditions, not just a well-known name.

### Can I get around without a car?

Yes. You can base your trip in one district and use local transport or transfers. A car or prearranged rides are more convenient if you frequently switch beaches, since crossing the island can take significant time.

### How many days does the island need?

A short stop is enough to discover one area. To explore different shores, the lagoon and the historic center, allow several days. Check the duration of specific itineraries in the [Brazil tours catalog](/brazil/tour/).

### Is Florianópolis only a beach destination?

No. It also offers dunes, lagoons, historic neighborhoods, fishing culture and walking routes through nature. If several activities interest you, plan them by district and expected weather.

## Tours featuring Florianópolis: several island days or a journey's finale

[Florianópolis](/brazil/place/florianopolis/) is the capital of Santa Catarina state, spread across an island and the adjoining mainland coast. After mountain roads and waterfalls, the setting changes to ocean beaches, lagoons, dunes and the chance to enjoy a day without excursions.

The Ada Tours catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Florianópolis on the **main itinerary**. The key question is how long you will actually stay on the island. Arriving in the evening and spending several nights on the coast are very different experiences, even if both tours list “Florianópolis.”

Read the [Florianópolis destination guide](/brazil/place/florianopolis/) for its landscapes, beaches and city attractions. Here you can compare itineraries that stop there. More destinations appear in the [Brazil tours catalog](/brazil/tour/), and sea-focused routes in the [Brazil beach holiday selection](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/).

## Two confirmed itinerary formats via Florianópolis

### Southern Brazil in 12 days: several days at the end

[“Southern Brazil in 12 Days”](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-rio-iguazu-gramado-florianopolis-12-days/) starts in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), visits Iguazu Falls, [Gramado](/brazil/place/gramado/) and [Canela](/brazil/place/canela/), then travels toward the canyons and ocean. This is a good option for a first introduction to different parts of the country, ending a busy journey with time on the coast.

On **day 9**, travelers arrive in Florianópolis and check into a hotel. **Day 10** features a city tour: 15 de Novembro Square, Cruz e Sousa Palace, Hercílio Luz Bridge and [Lagoa da Conceição](/brazil/place/lagoa-da-conceicao/). **Day 11** is free for the beach, walks and relaxation. **Day 12** brings a transfer to the airport.

There is therefore both a full sightseeing day and some free time. If beaches are the main reason for your visit, consider whether one free day is enough in the context of a larger journey.

### Southern Brazil VIP in 7 days: helicopter to the coast and a city tour

[“Southern Brazil VIP: Vineyards, Canyons and Ocean”](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-vip-7-days/) follows a different plan. It begins in [Porto Alegre](/brazil/place/porto-alegre/), passes through [Bento Gonçalves](/brazil/place/bento-goncalves/), Gramado and [Cambará do Sul](/brazil/place/cambara-do-sul/). The confirmed program includes [Itaimbezinho Canyon](/brazil/place/itaimbezinho-canyon/), a hot-air balloon flight and other activities.

On **day 6**, a private helicopter flight takes travelers from Cambará do Sul to Florianópolis, where they meet an English-speaking guide and check into a hotel. **Day 7** includes a private city sightseeing tour followed by an airport transfer. The journey itself from the mountains to the ocean is a highlight of this itinerary. There is less time for an extended independent beach holiday.

The VIP name alone does not establish which services are guaranteed. However, **the private helicopter flight** is expressly listed as included on this particular itinerary. Accommodation, exclusions and prices are detailed on the [7-day tour page](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-vip-7-days/).

| Itinerary | Role of Florianópolis |
|---|---|
| [12-day Southern Brazil trip](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-rio-iguazu-gramado-florianopolis-12-days/) | Arrival, sightseeing day, free day and departure |
| [7-day VIP trip](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-vip-7-days/) | Helicopter arrival, overnight stay, sightseeing and departure |

## Which excursions are actually included on the island?

On the 12-day journey, the excursion visits specific city landmarks. 15 de Novembro Square and Cruz e Sousa Palace introduce the capital's history, Hercílio Luz Bridge illustrates its island geography, and [Lagoa da Conceição](/brazil/place/lagoa-da-conceicao/) adds a natural landscape.

The VIP itinerary confirms a **private sightseeing tour**, but its description does not name the same list of stops. Do not simply carry the day-ten itinerary from the other tour into this one: the [VIP journey's own itinerary](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-vip-7-days/) determines which places are visited.

Beyond scheduled stops, the island is known for Joaquina, Mole and Campeche beaches, dunes and coastal walks. Florianópolis municipal materials separately describe the protected dune area of Lagoa da Conceição, fishing communities and coastal ecosystems. These are ideas for a free day or a customized extension, **not a list of excursions already paid for** on both tours.

If you enjoy outdoor activities, compare [adventure tours in Brazil](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/). For coastal relaxation, see the [beach holiday selection](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/).

## Connecting the island with mountains, waterfalls and other cities

Florianópolis is a considerable distance from Rio and Iguazu. The 12-day itinerary connects them through flights and overland travel; **the Rio–Iguazu–Porto Alegre domestic flight segment** appears among services excluded from the base price. Factor this cost into comparisons of itineraries with different transport arrangements.

On the seven-day VIP journey, the emphasis shifts to the wine region, canyons and a private helicopter flight. Flying reduces the road journey between the mountain section and the coast, although operation depends on flying conditions. The tour ends in Florianópolis, so onward connections should be planned around flight schedules.

For more mountains and scenic trails, explore [tours via Cambará do Sul](/brazil/place/cambara-do-sul/tour/) and the [Itaimbezinho Canyon guide](/brazil/place/itaimbezinho-canyon/). If the sea is your priority, choose an itinerary with a separate free day or discuss extending your stay.

## Season and preparation

Southern Hemisphere summer, especially December–February, suits travelers primarily interested in beach days. Heavy rain and high demand in popular coastal areas are possible at this time. Autumn and spring are also appealing for city walks, lagoons and dunes, although the sea may be cooler. On a journey involving canyons, the weather on the coast and high plateau may differ considerably on the same day.

Comfortable light shoes are useful for city sightseeing; exposed dunes call for sun protection, water and attention to the wind. Allow travel time when changing between distant beaches: the island is long, and hills and urban development separate its bays.

When choosing a tour, focus first on **the number of days actually spent in Florianópolis**, whether there is a free beach day, the time available for sightseeing and the onward flight.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Florianópolis

### Is there a tour with time to relax without excursions?

Yes. On the [12-day program](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-rio-iguazu-gramado-florianopolis-12-days/), **day 11 is free**. You can spend it by the ocean or exploring independently.

### Which tour includes a helicopter flight to the island?

The [7-day VIP itinerary](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-vip-7-days/) includes a private flight from Cambará do Sul on day six. It is a feature of that particular itinerary, not a standard element of every VIP tour.

### Are surfing and dune activities included in the price?

Neither is listed as a separate included service on the two itineraries compared here. Consider them for free time, subject to confirming arrangements and conditions.

### Can Florianópolis be combined with Iguazu Falls?

Yes. The [12-day itinerary](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-rio-iguazu-gramado-florianopolis-12-days/) includes [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) before traveling through the southern states and reaching the island. The seven-day VIP itinerary focuses on the canyons as its main nature experience.

### Which itinerary provides a longer stay beside the ocean?

Of these two, the **12-day tour** allows more island time. If you want to spend most of the holiday by the sea, compare options in the [Brazil beach tours catalog](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/) and check the number of free days.

## Fortaleza Canyon: sweeping Serra Geral views in southern Brazil

Fortaleza is a canyon in Serra Geral National Park in southern Brazil, near [Cambará do Sul](/brazil/place/cambara-do-sul/). High rock walls rise above a wide green valley. The upper plateau offers long-range views of curving cliffs, open grassland and forested slopes.

Fortaleza's defining quality is a sense of open space. It is rewarding to walk along accessible upper trails and gradually change your perspective on the cliff line. The panorama depends heavily on visibility, however: fog and low clouds can hide the distant sections even while some nearby rocks remain visible.

## Where Fortaleza is and how to get there

The canyon lies within the protected Serra Geral area near Cambará do Sul, in Rio Grande do Sul state. Visitors reach trailheads by roads across the plateau. Some access roads are unpaved, so allow for road surface conditions, weather and the exact starting point when estimating travel time.

The name can be confusing. **Fortaleza Canyon in southern Brazil has no geographical connection to the city of Fortaleza** on the northeastern coast, in Ceará state. They are entirely different places. Search for park admission, excursions, transport and travel times specifically for the Serra Geral canyon.

## Fortaleza versus Itaimbezinho

Nearby [Itaimbezinho Canyon](/brazil/place/itaimbezinho-canyon/) is known for its narrow, deep gorge and almost vertical walls. Fortaleza offers broader, extended panoramas with multiple cliff lines running into vegetated valleys.

| Fortaleza | Itaimbezinho |
|---|---|
| Wide valley panoramas | Narrow gorge |
| Serra Geral National Park | Aparados da Serra National Park |

Even after seeing Itaimbezinho, Fortaleza merits its own visit because the natural scenery differs considerably. If time is short, decide based on weather, the length of walk you want and whether you prefer an open panorama or views into a narrow, deep canyon.

## Viewpoints and walking routes

One of the area's best-known viewpoints is Mirante do Fortaleza. From here, look at how the line of the rocky rim unfolds from nearby cliffs into long valleys. Official national park tourism information also mentions Pedra do Segredo in the area of natural walking routes.

Each section has its own length and access conditions. A relaxed stop at a viewpoint and a full walk along the plateau edge require different amounts of time. Park authorities may temporarily restrict routes because of weather, trail conditions or conservation measures.

Distinguish between **an accessible viewpoint** and an independent excursion along an unprepared cliff edge. The canyon has significant drops, the wind can be strong and paths may be wet. Follow official markers and do not approach unfenced edges for a photograph.

## How much time should you allow?

For a first visit, it is convenient to allocate a separate day from [Cambará do Sul](/brazil/place/cambara-do-sul/), including driving time and walks on the upper trails. With less time available, focus on the main viewpoints, subject to current visiting hours.

A **2-day canyon trip** is generally easier to organize with 1 day in Serra Geral and 1 day in Aparados da Serra. This leaves an opportunity to reverse the order if clouds obscure one of the views. For a long trek, check its actual duration and whether guiding is mandatory.

This is general advice for planning a nature excursion, not an existing Ada Tours commercial offer. Explore the [Brazil tours section](/brazil/tour/) and check the specific itinerary for confirmed inclusion of Fortaleza and visiting conditions.

## When are the panoramas best?

There is no fixed time when the high plateau is guaranteed to be cloud-free. Sometimes the views are completely open in the morning before fog arrives; on other days, the clear window comes in the afternoon. Local visibility forecasts and actual conditions at the park entrance are therefore more useful than generic promises of an “ideal season.”

Sun and wind also change how the landscape looks. Bring water, shoes with good grip, a warm layer and rain protection for a walk. In heavy fog, the viewpoint may remain accessible even though the long-distance panorama is entirely hidden.

## Combining Fortaleza with nearby sites

Fortaleza's closest major natural counterpart is [Itaimbezinho](/brazil/place/itaimbezinho-canyon/). [Cambará do Sul](/brazil/place/cambara-do-sul/) is a convenient base for accommodation and travel arrangements. This route focuses on highland scenery, canyons and walking.

For a longer journey through Brazil, compare other themed itineraries in [“Adventure”](/interests/adventure/) and nature trips under [“Nature”](/interests/nature/). A shared theme does not mean every trip visits Fortaleza.

## Frequently asked questions about Fortaleza Canyon

### Is Fortaleza Canyon near the city of Fortaleza?

No. The canyon is in southern Brazil, near Cambará do Sul in Serra Geral National Park. The city with the same name is far away on Brazil's northeastern Atlantic coast.

### How does Fortaleza differ from Itaimbezinho?

Fortaleza offers broader views of valleys, whereas Itaimbezinho provides a dramatic view into a narrow, deep gorge. They are distinct natural experiences; visit both if time permits.

### How much time is needed for Fortaleza?

It is easiest to plan a separate day including the drive from Cambará do Sul, viewpoint stops and walks on permitted routes. Exact duration depends on available trails and road conditions.

### Can you see the canyon in fog?

Some viewpoints may still be reachable, but distant views can be completely obscured. Follow park rules and avoid unmarked trails in poor visibility.

### Should park admission and access rules be checked in advance?

Yes. Operating hours, admission arrangements and the condition of roads and trails may change. Use current information from Serra Geral park authorities rather than a previous year's visitor schedule.

## Tours through Fortaleza Canyon: seeing the cliffs of southern Brazil

[Fortaleza Canyon](/brazil/place/fortaleza-canyon/) lies in Serra Geral National Park near [Cambará do Sul](/brazil/place/cambara-do-sul/). It is known for its long rock walls and broad views across a green valley. The perspective from above is central to the visit: walking along the plateau allows you to appreciate the gorge in its entirety when cloud and fog do not obscure the opposite slopes.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include Fortaleza on their **main itinerary**. This catalog helps you choose a trip with a confirmed canyon visit. The [Fortaleza destination guide](/brazil/place/fortaleza-canyon/) describes its history and geography in more detail. This is not the large city of Fortaleza on Brazil's northeastern coast; it is a natural attraction in the southern states.

## Which Ada Tours itinerary includes Fortaleza?

On the [13-day Brazil tour via Rio, the Pantanal, Bonito, Iguazu and the southern states](/brazil/tour/brazil-iguazu-pantanal-bonito-porto-alegre-13-days/), Fortaleza Canyon is part of the main route. The journey begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), continues to the [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/) to discover its wetland ecosystems and then to [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/), where clear rivers and caves feature in the itinerary.

The next major stop is [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The journey then continues to [Porto Alegre](/brazil/place/porto-alegre/) and [Bento Gonçalves](/brazil/place/bento-goncalves/), with its wine-country scenery. Only then does it reach the high plateau near Cambará do Sul.

This is an important feature of the tour: **Fortaleza is not a separate multi-day expedition**. It is a highlight of the southern nature section of a much wider journey through Brazil. If the canyons are your principal reason for traveling, compare the days actually spent around Cambará do Sul, not just the tour's total length.

## What is planned for day 12?

On the thirteen-day program, **day 12** covers Cambará do Sul and two canyons: [Itaimbezinho](/brazil/place/itaimbezinho-canyon/) and [Fortaleza](/brazil/place/fortaleza-canyon/). A helicopter flight to the canyon area is planned for this day, along with walks on trails to scenic viewpoints and the opportunity to see the cliffs from the air.

The same itinerary describes a picnic stop near the canyon rim with wine, fresh fruit and chocolate from Gramado. After the nature excursions, a transfer to the **Parador Casa da Montanha** hotel is scheduled. The following day, the route heads back toward Porto Alegre Airport.

These features belong to **this specific thirteen-day program**, not to every visit to the national park. The exact order of walks, stopping place and feasibility of the helicopter leg depend on how the day is arranged and actual conditions. Check which services are paid for in the tour's own [“Included” and “Not Included” sections](/brazil/tour/brazil-iguazu-pantanal-bonito-porto-alegre-13-days/), where accommodation, excursions, transfers and domestic flights are listed separately.

## Fortaleza and Itaimbezinho: why visit both?

Both canyons lie within the Aparados da Serra and Serra Geral protected-area system, but they feel different. Fortaleza is characterized by open space, a long plateau rim and wide views of the valley and cliffs. [Itaimbezinho](/brazil/place/itaimbezinho-canyon/) is known for its narrow, steep cuts through the plateau and viewpoints that reveal the depth of the gorge.

| Place | Main characteristic |
|---|---|
| [Fortaleza](/brazil/place/fortaleza-canyon/) | Broad, extended panoramas of the rock walls |
| [Itaimbezinho](/brazil/place/itaimbezinho-canyon/) | Narrow, deep canyon and distinct viewpoints |

Brazil's conservation institute ICMBio lists routes to the Fortaleza lookout, Pedra do Segredo and along canyon edges within Serra Geral National Park. These describe **the park's options**, not a promise to complete all three routes on a single Ada Tours day.

If the geography of the region is your principal interest, begin by exploring [Cambará do Sul](/brazil/place/cambara-do-sul/) and then both canyons. To compare broader journeys, visit [Brazil adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/) and [routes via Cambará do Sul](/brazil/place/cambara-do-sul/tour/).

## Who is a tour visiting Fortaleza suitable for?

**Travelers seeking several different regions of Brazil.** The program combines city excursions, the natural areas of the [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/) and [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/), Iguazu Falls and southern rocky plateaus. There are several journeys between distant parts of the country, but the canyons become part of a rich, varied itinerary.

**Travelers interested in views from the plateau rim.** Fortaleza's defining experience is its panoramas. For ordinary scenic walks, comfortable shoes and the ability to walk across open terrain are important. Do not assume a long, strenuous trek is a compulsory part of this tour: its specific itinerary describes walks to viewpoints.

**Travelers attracted to unusual transportation.** A helicopter and picnic are mentioned on the canyon day, but these details belong to the specific program and need to be compared with its terms. A different [7-day Southern Brazil VIP tour](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-vip-7-days/) visits Itaimbezinho, but that does not mean Fortaleza is included there too. For a confirmed Fortaleza visit, use the selection on this page.

## Weather, fog and safety on the plateau

Cloud and visibility change rapidly around Cambará do Sul. The distant part of the canyon may disappear into fog even after a clear spell. As wide views are central to a Fortaleza visit, allowing flexibility for weather matters more than rigidly scheduling the experience for a particular hour.

The exposed plateau can be windy. Pack rain protection, a warm layer and shoes with good grip. Do not approach an unfenced cliff edge for photos, particularly in strong wind, wet grass or fog. The national park administration sets trail access rules and weather-related restrictions, which may change.

The region lies considerably farther south than Brazil's tropical areas. Clothes suitable for [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) may not be warm enough on the plateau. Account for that contrast when packing for a multi-day itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about Fortaleza Canyon tours

### Does Ada Tours have an itinerary that definitely visits Fortaleza?

Yes. On the [13-day Brazil tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-iguazu-pantanal-bonito-porto-alegre-13-days/), Fortaleza is listed among the main destinations and in the day-twelve description, alongside Itaimbezinho.

### Are Fortaleza Canyon and the city of Fortaleza the same place?

No. The canyon is near [Cambará do Sul](/brazil/place/cambara-do-sul/) in southern Brazil. The city of the same name is on Brazil's northeastern coast. For this nature journey, choose [Fortaleza Canyon](/brazil/place/fortaleza-canyon/).

### Can Fortaleza and Itaimbezinho be seen on one trip?

Yes. Both appear on day 12 of the confirmed thirteen-day itinerary. The exact sequence, walking routes and time at each viewpoint depend on conditions on the day.

### How much time should I allocate to the canyon?

On the named tour, the canyons form part of one planned day. If you want to hike several separate trails, watch sunrises or spend longer on the plateau, consider a longer stay in the region rather than assuming all of this can be fitted into a standard sightseeing stop.

### Are views of the cliffs guaranteed?

No. Fog and low clouds are characteristic of the region. Build some flexibility into the route and follow current park rules and your guides' instructions.
